chunks: And by this chain of narrators, from Muhammad ibn Uthman, he said: Narrated to us Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Raqqi, he said: Narrated to us Isa ibn Yunus from Mujalid ibn Saeed from al-Sha'bi from Masruq, who said:

We were with Ibn Mas'ud when a man asked him: Did your Prophet inform you how many successors would be after him? He said: Yes. And no one else asked me about it before you, and indeed you are the youngest of the people in age. I heard him say: After me, there will be as many caliphs as there were chiefs of Musa (peace be upon him). Allah, the Mighty and High, said: '...and We raised up among them twelve chieftains...'
ai.seo_question: How many successors did the Prophet Muhammad predict for the Muslim community?
ai.summary: This narration from Ibn Mas'ud, recorded in Al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba*, establishes the number of twelve successors by linking them to the twelve chiefs (Nuqba') of the Children of Israel under Musa (AS). By citing Surah Al-A'raf, the hadith provides a Quranic precedent for this specific number, reinforcing the Shia doctrine of the Twelve Imams through a cross-referential theological argument that bridges Old Testament lineage with Islamic prophetic succession.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 97 - It is narrated from the same chains of narrators from Muhammad bin Uthman that: Narrated to us Abdullah bin Ja’far Raqqi that: Narrated to us Isa bin Yunus from Majalid bin Saeed from Shobi from Masruq [bin Ajda bin Malik Hamadani, died 63 A.H.] that:

I was with Ibn Masud when a person asked him: Did your Prophet inform you how many his successors would be? Ibn Masud said: Yes, in spite of the fact that you are the youngest, no one other than you asked me this question. I always heard the Messenger of Allah (s) say: After me there will be Caliphs equal to the number of the chiefs of Musa (a.s). Allah, the Mighty and the High said: “…and We raised up among them twelve chieftains…”
